incidents.vector: Infostealer malware (Vidar, Lumma, StealC, RedLine, Acreed, Atomic Stealer) on users' devices harvested Claude login sessions and cookies, bypassing MFA via session hijacking.
incidents.impact: An unknown number of Claude accounts were accessed and their usage allotments consumed; Anthropic force-signed out affected users, removed saved payment methods, and refunded unauthorized charges.

incidents.vector: ClickFix-style social engineering ("TerminalFix") using fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA overlays that trick users into pasting a malicious command into PowerShell, leading to DLL sideloading and payloads hidden in PNG images.
incidents.impact: Microsoft reports the campaign establishes encrypted reverse tunnels into enterprise networks, enabling privilege escalation, data exfiltration, and ransomware deployment in follow-on hands-on-keyboard activity.

incidents.vector: Distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack against government network infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Norway's government network was temporarily taken offline; a pro-Kremlin hacktivist group claimed responsibility.

incidents.vector: Voice-phishing ("Spring Ring") via external Microsoft Teams accounts posing as IT help desk, coercing employees to run remote-access tools or malware; one variant escalated to an NTLM relay attack against domain controllers.
incidents.impact: Coordinated January-April 2026 operation disclosed by Unit 42 targeted more than 150 employees across at least 10 organizations to gain enterprise network footholds via attacker-controlled Microsoft 365 tenants.

incidents.vector: Market manipulation — inflated the thinly traded Tonic token more than 100x in 20 minutes, then borrowed assets against the inflated collateral.
incidents.impact: At least $6 million stolen; an attempted $74 million outflow was largely blocked when the Cronos blockchain made an emergency halt and rolled back roughly $68 million still on-chain.

incidents.vector: Compromise of a third-party application, likely via social engineering and identity abuse, with a four-day data-theft intrusion beginning August 21.
incidents.impact: Data on customers in oncology, multispecialty and medical-surgical units stolen from the distributor of roughly one-third of North American pharmaceuticals; extortionists claim hundreds of millions of records and reportedly demand over $55 million with a September 1 deadline.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion of two Berlin ministries with data exfiltration between August 7 and 12, followed by an extortion demand.
incidents.impact: Attackers claim 5.79 TB of government data including contracts, emails and classified material, auctioned for 30 bitcoin; Berlin refused to pay, and affected ministries remain cut off from normal IT systems weeks before September 20 elections.

incidents.victim: Open-source software supply chain (thousands of businesses)
incidents.vector: Self-propagating worm embedded in open-source packages via phished or stolen developer credentials at GitHub and NPM, harvesting cloud keys and secrets downstream.
incidents.impact: Australian Federal Police arrested two alleged members of the group behind the longest-running software supply chain attack spree, which compromised an AI gateway used by 2,500+ organizations and 3,800+ GitHub repositories.

incidents.victim: Government and defense organizations in Romania, Spain, Türkiye
incidents.vector: Spearphishing with macro-enabled Word documents using diplomatic-themed lures that install a lightweight batch-script backdoor abusing legitimate webhook services for command-and-control.
incidents.impact: Initial-access campaigns from late September 2025 through early April 2026 targeted European diplomatic and defense-manufacturing entities for intelligence collection, including material tied to Moldova's parliamentary elections.

incidents.vector: Manipulation of the platform's MAMO token price to borrow assets with no effective collateral.
incidents.impact: $8.7 million in crypto-assets stolen; borrowing paused during investigation. This is the platform's fourth hack in twelve months.

incidents.victim: U.S. federal agencies and critical infrastructure
incidents.vector: Complementary hacking platforms that mass-infected internet-of-things devices and routed intrusions through an obfuscation proxy network to disguise their Chinese origin.
incidents.impact: DOJ and FBI seized the platforms' domains, disabling infrastructure a China-based contractor used against NASA, the Federal Reserve, DOE, DOJ, HHS, NIH and the U.S. Senate; activity dates back to at least 2018.

incidents.vector: Attack on company servers; the company has not disclosed the intrusion method.
incidents.impact: Six casinos closed for roughly three days with cash registers and hotel systems disrupted and some staff furloughed; reopening is gradual with table games, bingo and the loyalty system still unavailable.

incidents.vector: Internet scanning for exposed Siemens S7 programmable logic controllers, then AI-generated exploitation scripts disguised as legitimate monitoring tools to gain read/write access.
incidents.impact: NSA, CISA, FBI, DOE and EPA warn of active reconnaissance and capability development against U.S. manufacturing, energy, water, chemical and food-sector control systems, assessed as pre-positioning for future disruptive operations.

incidents.victim: Universities, companies and government agencies (US and allied)
incidents.vector: Coordinated spearphishing against more than 100,000 professor accounts to steal credentials and exfiltrate research data.
incidents.impact: DOJ unsealed a superseding indictment charging 17 members of an Iran-based hacking-for-hire institute that stole 31+ terabytes of academic data and IP from 322 universities, dozens of companies and government agencies; $10 million rewards offered for five defendants.

incidents.vector: Fraudulent remote-employment operations using 22+ fabricated personas with AI-generated photos, AI-assisted interview responses, and facilitators maintaining company-issued hardware.
incidents.impact: North Korean IT workers, likely operating from China, applied to over 1,100 companies and are assessed to be actively employed at ten or more organizations, posing an ongoing insider threat and funneling wages to the North Korean regime.

incidents.attacker: Criminal hacker — credential theft and resale
incidents.vector: Claimed use of compromised credentials via MFA-fatigue and password-spraying attacks to access Microsoft Entra tenants (claims not yet verified).
incidents.impact: An actor is offering allegedly stolen employee data from several high-profile organizations for sale on criminal forums following August 1-17 activity; Unit 42 recommends auditing remote-access logs for logins following large volumes of password failures.

incidents.vector: Near-autonomous AI attack using up to eight coordinated AI agents to crack credentials, find and exploit vulnerabilities, and install backdoors over 12 attack waves in four days — no zero-days required.
incidents.impact: Personnel records exfiltrated and persistent backdoors placed on government web applications in what researchers call the first near-autonomous AI attack on a nation-state; Taiwan's digital ministry confirmed the July attacks in mid-August.
